original_card.question: Can the 64-per-call centre path (eight rank-8 COPY/ERASE totals through the private temporary) be shared across calls or shrunk?
methods: Derive a fully charged favorable relaxation for sharing one centre path across k calls, including restoration, hosting and precision.
Prove a lower bound on copied information per call for the selected decoder contract.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Show the changed centre charge and copy profile per call with every added restoration or hosting cost charged, and its ceiling via ceiling.ceiling(centre=...). A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write the per-call centre charge and copy children for sharing across k = 2 calls, charge the sharing overhead, and screen it; stop this route if even the ideal sharing gains under 10%. Ideal budgets: free 2.80x, shared by two 1.90x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: The centre path consumes 64 of about 99.6 unpaid coordinates per call, i.e. about 64% of the raw deficit.
allowed_variations: One sharing pattern across a fixed number of calls.
One reduced copied-total contract for the existing decoder.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Removing copies without a replacement contract for the decoder's copied totals.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

PROVEN (README.md, written proofs): chi(Z) >= 4 requires chi(U(Z)) >= 4; chi(Z) <= 3 for v <= 4 (Lemma RK(a)); every G_0 neighbourhood spans at most 2 dimensions on each side; G_0 contains no odd wheel and G_0[N(t)] is empty (p(t) not parallel to q(t)) or a disjoint union of cliques of size <= 3 and complete bipartite graphs (two-plane classification); basis-pivot families q(t) parallel to basis vectors give tripartite Z (chi(Z) <= 3); and an explicit rank-3 decoder (6 lines) with chi(U(Z)) = 4 (underlying W5) but chi(Z) = 2, exact cert = 6 = v, separating the underlying-graph question from the dichromatic one. DEMOTED / OPEN: chi(Z) <= 3 for all rank-3 zero digraphs is NOT proved; the search is bounded in v and in construction budgets; chi(Z) >= 4 is not shown impossible. No 'exactly when' or necessity claim; chain values are bounded-search upper bounds; the recorded fixture limits 11/18 rest on PR 2111's recorded CP-SAT optimality, not re-verified here. open_questions.question: Is chi(Z) <= 3 forced for every rank-3 zero digraph with nonzero diagonal? Equivalently: can chi(Z) >= 4 happen at rank 3 at all?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If forced, residue (ii) reduces entirely to the D(t)-compatible question PR 2774 settled on the fixtures, and the digraph-coloring half of the residue disappears. If not, the minimal fixture would name the obstruction a class-(ii) proof must overcome beyond the pivot constraints.
open_questions.first_step: Exhaustive pattern search at v = 5..6 over all realizable (pi, sigma, Z) with exact rank-3 realization tests (determinantal constraints), or a proof that the two-plane neighbourhood classification plus Lemma RK force a 3-colouring.
open_questions.blocked_by: No structural contradiction found; the sequential linear construction of the smallest triangle-free 4-chromatic target stalls at 6-8 of 11 vertices under 60000-200000 node budgets, which is not a proof.

open_questions.question: Does chi(Z) >= 4 (if realizable) force cert(M) < floor(2v/3), or can anchor/MX labellings still certify?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It separates a combinatorial digraph obstruction from an actual F-star falsifier. The chi(U) = 4 / chi(Z) = 2 separation example shows the underlying graph alone never decides cert; the fixtures show chi(Z) = 3 with cert = v.
open_questions.first_step: On any future chi(Z) >= 4 fixture, compute anchor reach |S_gamma|, matched-pivot value and exact cert where a-enumeration terminates; the settlement machinery of verify.py (settle()) already reports exactly these quantities.
